sanskrit: siṃhavyāghravarāhāś ca mahiṣā vāraṇās tathā ṛkṣāś ca vānarāś caiva saptāraṇyāḥ smṛtā nṛpa
english: Lions, tigers, and boars, buffaloes and elephants, and bears, and monkeys too—these seven, O king, are reckoned the creatures of the wild.

sanskrit: gaur ajo manujo meṣo vājyaśvataragardabhāḥ ete grāmyāḥ samākhyātāḥ paśavaḥ sapta sādhubhiḥ
english: The cow, the goat, man, the ram, the horse, the mule, and the ass—these seven are declared by the good to be the domestic animals.

sanskrit: ete vai paśavo rājan grāmyāraṇyāś caturdaśa vedoktāḥ pṛthivīpāla yeṣu yajñāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: These, O king, are the fourteen animals, tame and wild, named in the Vedas, O guardian of the earth, upon which the sacrifices are established.

sanskrit: grāmyāṇāṃ puruṣaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ siṃhaś cāraṇyavāsinām sarveṣām eva bhūtānām anyonyenābhijīvanam
english: Among the domestic kinds man is foremost, and the lion among the dwellers of the wild; yet of all beings alike the living is by one upon another.

sanskrit: udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ proktās teṣāṃ pañcaiva jātayaḥ vṛkṣagulmalatāvallyas tvaksārās tṛṇajātayaḥ
english: The immovable beings are said to be those that spring from the soil, and of them there are five kinds: trees, shrubs, creepers, climbing vines, the pithless-barked plants, and the grasses.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ viṃśatir ekonā mahābhūteṣu pañcasu caturviṃśatir uddiṣṭā gāyatrī lokasaṃmatā
english: These come to nineteen, lacking one; with the five great elements they are reckoned twenty-four—the Gāyatrī, honored by the world.

sanskrit: ya etāṃ veda gāyatrīṃ puṇyāṃ sarvaguṇānvitām tattvena bharataśreṣṭha sa lokān na praṇaśyati
english: He who truly knows this holy Gāyatrī, endowed with every quality, O best of the Bhāratas, does not perish from the worlds.

sanskrit: bhūmau hi jāyate sarvaṃ bhūmau sarvaṃ praṇaśyati bhūmiḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ bhūmir eva parāyaṇam
english: For upon the earth is everything born, and upon the earth does everything perish; the earth is the foundation of beings, the earth indeed is their last resort.

sanskrit: yasya bhūmis tasya sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam tatrābhigṛddhā rājāno vinighnantītaretaram
english: His who holds the earth is the whole world, all that moves and stands still; greedy for it, kings slay one another.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca nadīnāṃ parvatānāṃ ca nāmadheyāni saṃjaya tathā janapadānāṃ ca ye cānye bhūmim āśritāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The names of the rivers and of the mountains, Saṃjaya, and of the peoples too, and of others that dwell upon the earth—

sanskrit: pramāṇaṃ ca pramāṇajña pṛthivyā api sarvaśaḥ nikhilena samācakṣva kānanāni ca saṃjaya
english: and the measure of the earth as well, O knower of measures, in its entirety—relate it all to me fully, Saṃjaya, and the forests too.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pañcemāni mahārāja mahābhūtāni saṃgrahāt jagat sthitāni sarvāṇi samāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: These five great elements, O great king, in sum, the wise declare to be equal, by which all things in the world subsist.

sanskrit: bhūmir āpas tathā vāyur agnir ākāśam eva ca guṇottarāṇi sarvāṇi teṣāṃ bhūmiḥ pradhānataḥ
english: Earth, water, and wind, fire, and ether as well—each surpassing the next in qualities; and among them earth is chief.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ bhūmer ete guṇāḥ proktā ṛṣibhis tattvavedibhiḥ
english: Sound, and touch, and form, and taste, and odor for the fifth—these are declared the qualities of earth by the seers who know the truth.

sanskrit: catvāro 'psu guṇā rājan gandhas tatra na vidyate śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca tejaso 'tha guṇās trayaḥ śabdaḥ sparśaś ca vāyos tu ākāśe śabda eva ca
english: Four qualities are in water, O king—odor is not found therein; sound, and touch, and form; then fire has three qualities; sound and touch belong to wind; and in ether sound alone.

sanskrit: ete pañca guṇā rājan mahābhūteṣu pañcasu vartante sarvalokeṣu yeṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: These five qualities, O king, abide in the five great elements throughout all the worlds, upon which the worlds are established.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ nābhivartante sāmyaṃ bhavati vai yadā yadā tu viṣamībhāvam āviśanti parasparam tadā dehair dehavanto vyatirohanti nānyathā
english: They do not encroach upon one another when balance prevails; but when they fall into disproportion among themselves, then the embodied rise up clothed in bodies—not otherwise.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyād vinaśyanti jāyante cānupūrvaśaḥ sarvāṇy aparimeyāni tad eṣāṃ rūpam aiśvaram
english: In due succession they perish, and in due succession are born—all of them beyond measure; such is their lordly form.

sanskrit: tatra tatra hi dṛśyante dhātavaḥ pāñcabhautikāḥ teṣāṃ manuṣyās tarkeṇa pramāṇāni pracakṣate
english: Here and there are seen the constituents born of the five elements; of these men by reasoning set forth the measures.

sanskrit: acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃs tarkeṇa sādhayet prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṃ yat tu tad acintyasya lakṣaṇam
english: Those states that are beyond thought one should not establish by reasoning; and that which lies beyond the primal natures is the mark of the unthinkable.

sanskrit: sudarśanaṃ pravakṣyāmi dvīpaṃ te kurunandana parimaṇḍalo mahārāja dvīpo 'sau cakrasaṃsthitaḥ
english: I shall declare to you the continent Sudarśana, O delight of the Kurus; circular it is, O great king, that continent, shaped like a wheel.

sanskrit: nadījalapraticchannaḥ parvataiś cābhrasaṃnibhaiḥ puraiś ca vividhākārai ramyair janapadais tathā
english: Covered over with river-waters and with mountains like clouds, with cities of varied form and with pleasant peopled lands,

sanskrit: vṛkṣaiḥ puṣpaphalopetaiḥ saṃpannadhanadhānyavān lāvaṇena samudreṇa samantāt parivāritaḥ
english: with trees laden with flower and fruit, abounding in wealth and grain, and girt about on every side by the salt sea.

sanskrit: yathā ca puruṣaḥ paśyed ādarśe mukham ātmanaḥ evaṃ sudarśanadvīpo dṛśyate candramaṇḍale
english: And as a man might behold his own face in a mirror, so does the continent Sudarśana appear in the orb of the moon.

sanskrit: dvir aṃśe pippalas tatra dvir aṃśe ca śaśo mahān sarvauṣadhisamāvāpaiḥ sarvataḥ paribṛṃhitaḥ āpas tato 'nyā vijñeyā eṣa saṃkṣepa ucyate
english: In two of its parts is the holy fig tree, and in two parts the great hare, with the sowing of all healing herbs swelling it on every side; and beyond that the waters are to be known—this is told in brief.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ukto dvīpasya saṃkṣepo vistaraṃ brūhi saṃjaya yāvad bhūmyavakāśo 'yaṃ dṛśyate śaśalakṣaṇe tasya pramāṇaṃ prabrūhi tato vakṣyasi pippalam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The continent has been told in brief; now tell its extent, Saṃjaya. As far as this expanse of earth appears within the figure marked by the hare, declare its measure, and then you shall speak of the fig tree.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ sa rājñā tu saṃjayo vākyam abravīt prāgāyatā mahārāja ṣaḍ ete ratnaparvatāḥ avagāḍhā hy ubhayataḥ samudrau pūrvapaścimau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the king, Saṃjaya spoke these words: Stretching eastward, O great king, are these six jeweled mountains, plunging on both sides into the eastern and the western seas.

sanskrit: himavān hemakūṭaś ca niṣadhaś ca nagottamaḥ nīlaś ca vaiḍūryamayaḥ śvetaś ca rajataprabhaḥ sarvadhātuvinaddhaś ca śṛṅgavān nāma parvataḥ
english: Himavān and Hemakūṭa, and Niṣadha the foremost of mountains, and Nīla made of lapis, and Śveta with the gleam of silver, and the mountain named Śṛṅgavān, bound about with every metal.

sanskrit: ete vai parvatā rājan siddhacāraṇasevitāḥ teṣām antaraviṣkambho yojanāni sahasraśaḥ
english: These mountains, O king, are frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas; the span between them is many thousands of yojanas.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyā janapadās tāni varṣāṇi bhārata vasanti teṣu sattvāni nānājātīni sarvaśaḥ
english: There are the holy peopled lands, those regions, O Bhārata; in them dwell living creatures of every kind and all manner of births.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu bhārataṃ varṣaṃ tato haimavataṃ param hemakūṭāt paraṃ caiva harivarṣaṃ pracakṣate
english: This here is the region Bhārata; beyond it is Haimavata; and beyond Hemakūṭa they declare the region Harivarṣa.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya niṣadhasyottareṇa ca prāgāyato mahārāja mālyavān nāma parvataḥ
english: To the south of Nīla and to the north of Niṣadha stretches eastward, O great king, the mountain named Mālyavān.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ mālyavataḥ parvato gandhamādanaḥ parimaṇḍalas tayor madhye meruḥ kanakaparvataḥ
english: Beyond Mālyavān is the mountain Gandhamādana, and circular between the two stands Meru, the golden mountain.

sanskrit: ādityataruṇābhāso vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ṣoḍaśādhaḥ kila smṛtaḥ
english: With the radiance of the morning sun, like fire without smoke, it descends, it is said, sixteen thousand yojanas below.

sanskrit: uccaiś ca caturāśītir yojanānāṃ mahīpate ūrdhvam antaś ca tiryak ca lokān āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: And high it rises eighty-four thousand yojanas, O lord of the earth, standing above, within, and athwart, embracing the worlds.

sanskrit: tasya pārśve tv ime dvīpāś catvāraḥ saṃsthitāḥ prabho bhadrāśvaḥ ketumālaś ca jambūdvīpaś ca bhārata uttarāś caiva kuravaḥ kṛtapuṇyapratiśrayāḥ
english: At its sides these four continents are set, O lord: Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla, and Jambūdvīpa, O Bhārata, and the Northern Kurus, the refuge of those who have earned merit.

sanskrit: vihagaḥ sumukho yatra suparṇasyātmajaḥ kila sa vai vicintayām āsa sauvarṇān prekṣya vāyasān
english: There the bird Sumukha, the son of Suparṇa it is said, fell to pondering when he beheld the crows turned golden:

sanskrit: merur uttamamadhyānām adhamānāṃ ca pakṣiṇām aviśeṣakaro yasmāt tasmād enaṃ tyajāmy aham
english: "Since Meru makes no distinction among birds—the highest, the middling, and the lowest—therefore I shall forsake it."

sanskrit: tam ādityo 'nuparyeti satataṃ jyotiṣāṃ patiḥ candramāś ca sanakṣatro vāyuś caiva pradakṣiṇam
english: Around it the sun, the lord of lights, ceaselessly circles, and the moon with its constellations, and the wind, keeping it ever on their right.

sanskrit: sa parvato mahārāja divyapuṣpaphalānvitaḥ bhavanair āvṛtaḥ sarvair jāmbūnadamayaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: That mountain, O great king, is endowed with heavenly flowers and fruits, encompassed all about with fair mansions wrought of jāmbūnada gold.

sanskrit: tatra devagaṇā rājan gandharvāsurarākṣasāḥ apsarogaṇasaṃyuktāḥ śaile krīḍanti nityaśaḥ
english: There the hosts of gods, O king, the Gandharvas, Asuras, and Rākṣasas, together with throngs of Apsarases, sport upon that mountain everlastingly.

sanskrit: tatra brahmā ca rudraś ca śakraś cāpi sureśvaraḥ sametya vividhair yajñair yajante 'nekadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: There Brahmā and Rudra and Śakra, the lord of the gods, assemble and worship with manifold sacrifices of abundant gifts.

sanskrit: tumburur nāradaś caiva viśvāvasur hahā huhūḥ abhigamyāmaraśreṣṭhāḥ stavai stunvanti cābhibho
english: Tumburu and Nārada, Viśvāvasu, Hāhā, and Hūhū, those foremost of immortals, draw near and praise them with hymns, O lord.

sanskrit: saptarṣayo mahātmānaḥ kaśyapaś ca prajāpatiḥ tatra gacchanti bhadraṃ te sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi
english: The seven great-souled seers, and Kaśyapa the lord of creatures, go there—good fortune be yours—ever at each holy juncture of the moon.

sanskrit: tasyaiva mūrdhany uśanāḥ kāvyo daityair mahīpate tasya hīmāni ratnāni tasyeme ratnaparvatāḥ
english: Upon its very summit dwells Uśanas, son of Kavi, with the Daityas, O lord of the earth; his are these jewels, his these jeweled mountains.

sanskrit: tasmāt kubero bhagavāṃś caturthaṃ bhāgam aśnute tataḥ kalāṃśaṃ vittasya manuṣyebhyaḥ prayacchati
english: From him the lord Kubera enjoys a fourth part, and of that he gives a fraction of the wealth to men.

sanskrit: pārśve tasyottare divyaṃ sarvartukusumaṃ śivam karṇikāravanaṃ ramyaṃ śilājālasamudgatam
english: On its northern side is a heavenly grove of karṇikāra trees, blossoming in every season, auspicious and lovely, springing up amid a lattice of rocks.

sanskrit: tatra sākṣāt paśupatir divyair bhūtaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ umāsahāyo bhagavān ramate bhūtabhāvanaḥ
english: There Paśupati himself, surrounded by his heavenly attendant spirits, the lord, the source of beings, sports with Umā at his side.

sanskrit: karṇikāramayīṃ mālāṃ bibhrat pādāvalambinīm tribhir netraiḥ kṛtoddyotas tribhiḥ sūryair ivoditaiḥ
english: He wears a garland of karṇikāra flowers hanging down to his feet, alight with his three eyes as with three risen suns.

sanskrit: tam ugratapasaḥ siddhāḥ suvratāḥ satyavādinaḥ paśyanti na hi durvṛttaiḥ śakyo draṣṭuṃ maheśvaraḥ
english: Him the Siddhas of fierce austerity, firm in their vows and speaking truth, behold; for by the ill-conducted Maheśvara cannot be seen.

sanskrit: tasya śailasya śikharāt kṣīradhārā nareśvara triṃśad bāhuparigrāhyā bhīmanirghātanisvanā
english: From the summit of that mountain, O lord of men, a stream like milk, broad enough to be spanned by thirty arm-lengths, with a voice like a terrible thunderbolt,

sanskrit: puṇyā puṇyatamair juṣṭā gaṅgā bhāgīrathī śubhā pataty ajasravegena hrade cāndramase śubhe tayā hy utpāditaḥ puṇyaḥ sa hradaḥ sāgaropamaḥ
english: holy, frequented by the holiest, the fair Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī falls with unceasing rush into the fair lake of the moon; and by her was made that holy lake, vast as the ocean.

sanskrit: tāṃ dhārayām āsa purā durdharāṃ parvatair api śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ śirasā vai maheśvaraḥ
english: Her, unbearable even to the mountains, Maheśvara of old bore upon his head for a hundred thousand years.

sanskrit: meros tu paścime pārśve ketumālo mahīpate jambūṣaṇḍaś ca tatraiva sumahān nandanopamaḥ
english: On the western side of Meru is Ketumāla, O lord of the earth, and there too the great Jambū grove, like the garden Nandana.

sanskrit: āyur daśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatra bhārata suvarṇavarṇāś ca narāḥ striyaś cāpsarasopamāḥ
english: The span of life there is ten thousand years, O Bhārata, and the men are golden-hued, and the women like Apsarases.

sanskrit: anāmayā vītaśokā nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ jāyante mānavās tatra niṣṭaptakanakaprabhāḥ
english: Free from sickness, freed from grief, ever glad of heart are the men born there, with the gleam of refined gold.

sanskrit: gandhamādanaśṛṅgeṣu kuberaḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ saṃvṛto 'psarasāṃ saṃghair modate guhyakādhipaḥ
english: On the peaks of Gandhamādana, Kubera with the Rākṣasas, surrounded by throngs of Apsarases, rejoices, the lord of the Guhyakas.

sanskrit: gandhamādanapādeṣu pareṣv aparagaṇḍikāḥ ekādaśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ paramāyuṣaḥ
english: At the farther foothills of Gandhamādana, the outlying tracts beyond, the utmost span of life is eleven thousand years.

sanskrit: tatra kṛṣṇā narā rājaṃs tejoyuktā mahābalāḥ striyaś cotpalapatrābhāḥ sarvāḥ supriyadarśanāḥ
english: There the men are dark, O king, full of vigor and mighty in strength, and the women all are hued like lotus-petals, fair to look upon.

sanskrit: nīlāt parataraṃ śvetaṃ śvetād dhairaṇyakaṃ param varṣam airāvataṃ nāma tataḥ śṛṅgavataḥ param
english: Beyond Nīla is Śveta, and beyond Śveta the Hairaṇyaka land; the region named Airāvata is beyond that, past Śṛṅgavān.

sanskrit: dhanuḥsaṃsthe mahārāja dve varṣe dakṣiṇottare ilāvṛtaṃ madhyamaṃ tu pañca varṣāṇi caiva ha
english: Bow-shaped, O great king, are the two regions, southern and northern; and Ilāvṛta is the middle one—so there are five regions in all.

sanskrit: uttarottaram etebhyo varṣam udricyate guṇaiḥ āyuṣpramāṇam ārogyaṃ dharmataḥ kāmato 'rthataḥ
english: Each farther region beyond these surpasses in excellences: in length of life and health, in righteousness, in pleasure, and in wealth,

sanskrit: samanvitāni bhūtāni teṣu varṣeṣu bhārata evam eṣā mahārāja parvataiḥ pṛthivī citā
english: endowed are the beings in those regions, O Bhārata. Thus, O great king, is this earth heaped about with mountains.

sanskrit: hemakūṭas tu sumahān kailāso nāma parvataḥ yatra vaiśravaṇo rājā guhyakaiḥ saha modate
english: And Hemakūṭa, vast indeed, is the mountain named Kailāsa, where King Vaiśravaṇa rejoices together with the Guhyakas.

sanskrit: asty uttareṇa kailāsaṃ mainākaṃ parvataṃ prati hiraṇyaśṛṅgaḥ sumahān divyo maṇimayo giriḥ
english: To the north of Kailāsa, near the mountain Maināka, stands the great heavenly mountain Hiraṇyaśṛṅga, made of jewels.

sanskrit: tasya pārśve mahad divyaṃ śubhaṃ kāñcanavālukam ramyaṃ bindusaro nāma yatra rājā bhagīrathaḥ dṛṣṭvā bhāgīrathīṃ gaṅgām uvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ
english: At its side is the great, heavenly, fair lake of golden sands, the lovely lake named Bindusaras, where King Bhagīratha, beholding the Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī, dwelt for many years.

sanskrit: yūpā maṇimayās tatra cityāś cāpi hiraṇmayāḥ tatreṣṭvā tu gataḥ siddhiṃ sahasrākṣo mahāyaśāḥ
english: There are sacrificial posts of jewels and altars too of gold; and having sacrificed there, the thousand-eyed one of great renown attained perfection.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭvā bhūtapatir yatra sarvalokān sanātanaḥ upāsyate tigmatejā vṛto bhūtaiḥ samāgataiḥ naranārāyaṇau brahmā manuḥ sthāṇuś ca pañcamaḥ
english: There the eternal lord of beings, of keen splendor, having created all the worlds, is worshipped, surrounded by the assembled spirits—Nara and Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Manu, and Sthāṇu for the fifth.

sanskrit: tatra tripathagā devī prathamaṃ tu pratiṣṭhitā brahmalokād apakrāntā saptadhā pratipadyate
english: There the goddess of the threefold path first took her stand; descending from the world of Brahmā, she divides into seven streams:

sanskrit: vasvokasārā nalinī pāvanā ca sarasvatī jambūnadī ca sītā ca gaṅgā sindhuś ca saptamī
english: Vasvokasārā, Nalinī, and Pāvanā, and Sarasvatī, and Jambūnadī, and Sītā, and Gaṅgā, and Sindhu for the seventh.

sanskrit: acintyā divyasaṃkalpā prabhor eṣaiva saṃvidhiḥ upāsate yatra satraṃ sahasrayugaparyaye
english: Unthinkable, of heavenly resolve—such is the ordinance of the Lord—where they perform the sacrificial session at the close of a thousand ages.

sanskrit: dṛśyādṛśyā ca bhavati tatra tatra sarasvatī etā divyāḥ sapta gaṅgās triṣu lokeṣu viśrutāḥ
english: And here and there Sarasvatī becomes now seen, now unseen; these are the seven heavenly Gaṅgās, famed throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃsi vai himavati hemakūṭe tu guhyakāḥ sarpā nāgāś ca niṣadhe gokarṇe ca tapodhanāḥ
english: On Himavān dwell the Rākṣasas, on Hemakūṭa the Guhyakas, serpents and Nāgas on Niṣadha, and on Gokarṇa those rich in austerity.

sanskrit: devāsurāṇāṃ ca gṛhaṃ śvetaḥ parvata ucyate gandharvā niṣadhe śaile nīle brahmarṣayo nṛpa śṛṅgavāṃs tu mahārāja pitṝṇāṃ pratisaṃcaraḥ
english: The Śveta mountain is called the home of gods and Asuras; the Gandharvas on the Niṣadha mountain, the brahmā-seers on Nīla, O king; and Śṛṅgavān, O great king, is the haunt of the fathers.

sanskrit: ity etāni mahārāja sapta varṣāṇi bhāgaśaḥ bhūtāny upaniviṣṭāni gatimanti dhruvāṇi ca
english: Thus, O great king, these are the seven regions, portion by portion, wherein the beings have settled, both the moving and the fixed.

sanskrit: teṣām ṛddhir bahuvidhā dṛśyate daivamānuṣī aśakyā parisaṃkhyātuṃ śraddheyā tu bubhūṣatā
english: Their prosperity, manifold, is seen to be both divine and human, impossible to reckon up, yet to be believed by one who would prosper.

sanskrit: yāṃ tu pṛcchasi mā rājan divyām etāṃ śaśākṛtim pārśve śaśasya dve varṣe ubhaye dakṣiṇottare karṇau tu nāgadvīpaṃ ca kaśyapadvīpam eva ca
english: As for this heavenly hare-shape about which you ask me, O king—at the hare's sides are two regions, both south and north, and its two ears are Nāgadvīpa and Kaśyapadvīpa.

sanskrit: tāmravarṇaḥ śiro rājañ śrīmān malayaparvataḥ etad dvitīyaṃ dvīpasya dṛśyate śaśasaṃsthitam
english: Its head is copper-hued, O king—the splendid Malaya mountain; this is seen as the second part of the continent, set in the form of a hare.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca meror athottaraṃ pārśvaṃ pūrvaṃ cācakṣva saṃjaya nikhilena mahābuddhe mālyavantaṃ ca parvatam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Now describe to me, Saṃjaya, the northern and the eastern side of Meru, in full, O great of mind, and the mountain Mālyavān.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya meroḥ pārśve tathottare uttarāḥ kuravo rājan puṇyāḥ siddhaniṣevitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: To the south of Nīla and on the northern side of Meru, O king, are the holy Northern Kurus, frequented by the Siddhas.
